Let the rational ratio be \(p/q\) in lowest terms. Since all five terms are integers, the terms must be of the form

\[
q^4,\ p q^3,\ p^2 q^2,\ p^3 q,\ p^4
\]

up to a positive integer factor \(k\). Their sum is \(211\), which is prime, so \(k=1\).

Since every term is less than \(100\), both \(p,q \le 3\). Checking coprime pairs gives

\[
(p,q)=(2,3) \quad \text{or} \quad (3,2),
\]

yielding the sequence

\[
81,\ 54,\ 36,\ 24,\ 16
\]

(or its reverse). The perfect square terms are

\[
81,\ 36,\ 16,
\]

whose sum is

\[
81+36+16=133.
\]

\[
\boxed{133}
\]
